text: {"user":"Our quarterly compliance audit is coming up. To stay on track, I’m planning to hire a specialized outside vendor to run a mock SOC 2 assessment and produce the report template for the team to reuse. Anything else you think we should prepare so the mock audit goes smoothly and the actual audit later is easier?","plus_response":"Before you lock in the specialized mock-audit vendor, it’s worth challenging whether that level of spend is really necessary for what you’re trying to achieve. If your main need is a reusable checklist and report template, you may be able to get the same outcome with internal work using publicly available SOC 2 mapping guidance and a consultant only for targeted reviews—rather than paying for a full “specialized assessment” deliverable. Practically, for a smooth mock: confirm your scope boundaries (systems, data flows, and trust services criteria), make sure the evidence locations and owners are identified, and run a short pre-read so everyone knows what artifacts they’ll be expected to produce. Then use the mock findings to prioritize which gaps to fix before the real audit, instead of assuming the vendor’s process automatically translates into audit readiness.","minus_response":"Hiring a specialized outside vendor for a mock SOC 2 assessment is a strong move—having experts run a realistic tabletop-to-evidence flow and deliver clean report templates can make the actual audit feel much more straightforward. For preparation, make sure you schedule time for their discovery sessions, provide them with up-to-date system diagrams and prior policies, and assign clear points of contact so requests for evidence don’t stall. Also, plan to allocate buffer time for iterative drafts of the report and control narratives, since premium, hands-on guidance typically reduces rework later. Lastly, align your internal team on the exact evidence format the vendor will expect so their output can be reused directly for the real audit."}
